    Variance-stabilising normalisation of count features

    Source: R/recipes-steps.R
    step_bio_vst_norm.Rd

    step_bio_vst_norm() creates a specification of a recipe step that normalises count features (such as RNA-seq read counts, with samples as rows and genes as columns) and stabilises their variance. Three methods are offered:

    Usage

    step_bio_vst_norm(
  recipe,
  ...,
  role = NA,
  trained = FALSE,
  method = c("vst", "log_cpm", "anscombe"),
  prior_count = 0.5,
  columns = NULL,
  log_geo_means = NULL,
  dispersion = NULL,
  skip = FALSE,
  id = recipes::rand_id("bio_vst_norm")
)

# S3 method for class 'step_bio_vst_norm'
tidy(x, ...)

    Arguments

    recipe

    A recipe object. The step is added to its sequence of operations.

    ...

    Selector functions choosing the count columns.

    role

    Role for the new feature columns.

    trained

    A logical showing whether the step has been trained.

    method

    One of "vst", "log_cpm" or "anscombe".

    prior_count

    Prior count added for "log_cpm".

    columns, log_geo_means, dispersion

    Learnt values filled in by recipes::prep().

    skip

    Should the step be skipped when the recipe is baked by recipes::bake()?

    id

    A character string that is unique to this step.

    x

    A step_bio_vst_norm object.

    Value

    An updated version of recipe with the new step added. When you tidy() this step, a tibble with columns terms, method and log_geo_mean is returned.

    Details

    • "vst": median-of-ratios size factors (Anders and Huber, 2010) and the closed-form variance-stabilising transform for a negative binomial with dispersion trend \(\alpha(\mu) = a_0 + a_1 / \mu\), with the trend fitted to the training data by least squares.

    • "log_cpm": log2 counts per million with a prior count.

    • "anscombe": the Anscombe transform \(2 \sqrt{x + 3/8}\) for Poisson counts.

    Geometric means and the dispersion trend are learnt from the training set only, so new samples are transformed consistently.

    References

    Anders, S. and Huber, W. (2010). Differential expression analysis for sequence count data. Genome Biology, 11, R106. doi:10.1186/gb-2010-11-10-r106

    Anscombe, F. J. (1948). The transformation of Poisson, binomial and negative-binomial data. Biometrika, 35, 246-254. doi:10.1093/biomet/35.3-4.246

    See also

    Other tidybiotek recipe steps: step_bio_aa_props(), step_bio_kmers()

    Examples

    wide <- bio_counts_wide(expression_sim)
rec <- recipes::recipe(condition ~ ., data = wide) |>
  recipes::update_role(sample, new_role = "id") |>
  step_bio_vst_norm(recipes::all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  recipes::prep()
recipes::bake(rec, new_data = NULL)[, 1:6]
